subject: GPU reserve evaluation recap, success criteria and proposed milestones
messages:
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Alex Jones <alex.jones@nebulapay.com>
Cc: Priya Sharma <priya@nebulapay.com>
Date: 2026-04-11T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: GPU reserve evaluation recap, success criteria and proposed milestones

Hi Alex / Priya,

Thanks again for taking the time today — good conversation and helpful context. Below is a short recap to make sure we captured priorities and to propose concrete next steps so we can size a Dedicated (reserved GPU pool) pilot that maps to your requirements. Please correct anything I missed.

Quick recap of pain and goals
- Pain: erratic tail latency during peak batch windows; cost unpredictability when traffic spikes; need for isolation for payments-sensitive workloads (audit + limited cross-tenant access).
- Goal: predictable per-request latency and stable unit cost for inference; ability to guarantee isolation for regulated flows while supporting burst traffic for marketing spikes.

Current stack you described
- Serving: on-prem Kubernetes (GKE at present) with custom TF/torch stack and a homegrown request router.
- Model footprint: 30B-ish decoder models (quantized in-house prototypes), typical request ~256 tokens, occasional 1k token generation for reports.
- Observability: Prometheus + Grafana, but request-level cost visibility is limited.

Initial success criteria (what NebulaPay needs to validate)
- Latency SLO: p95 < 200ms for 256-token requests under steady 300 qps sustained load.
- Predictable throughput: sustain 300 qps steady, handle bursts to 1k qps for 30-60s with graceful degradation/fallback.
- Isolation: dedicated GPU pool with tenant isolation and audit logs, KMS integration for keys.
- Cost target: reduce per-token USD cost vs current self-hosted ops by >= 20% (ballpark).

Autoscaling / burst policy notes we discussed
- Prefer reserved pool sized for steady-state + short-lived burst buffer; burst policy to rely on queued requests + fast scale-up to warm cold-cache replicas.
- Need ability to define burst eligibility per route (payment-critical flows pinned to dedicated nodes).

Immediate next steps I propose
1) You share the scoping worksheet (I will attach a template) with expected QPS distribution, token histogram, and sample production prompts (redacted).
2) We run a short Dedicated POC: 2-week pilot using a 4-GPU reserved pool (we'll size precisely after you complete the sheet).
3) Redwood to provide: SOC2 summary, initial cost estimate, POC test plan, and a short MSA/POC addendum for legal.

Can you confirm the steady/burst QPS numbers and whether the p95 latency target above matches your bar? Also confirm the earliest week you could start a POC — my current availability for kickoff is the week of 2026-05-04.

Attachments: scoping template attached (nebulapay-scoping-sheet.xlsx) and SOC2 summary (SOC2-summary-2025.pdf).

Best,
Soojin
Principal Account Exec | Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0189

Thanks, Soojin — this is very helpful and captures the conversation. A couple clarifications and notes from our side: 

- Confirmed QPS: steady-state 300 qps (production), bursts to ~1,000 qps for campaign windows (typically 30–45s).
- Token profile: median ~200, 95th ~820, small subset of long-form reports we can exclude from POC if needed.
- Isolation: payment-processing routes must be isolated (separate pool or pinned instances) and we need KMS + audit log proof for SOC/PCI review.

We attached a filled scoping sheet (attached) with traffic histogram and sample prompt types. Also attaching our SOC questionnaire (we redacted PII). Can you give a ballpark monthly cost range for a reserved 4-GPU pool vs a 2-week pilot (we need a rough number for procurement)?

Procurement & timeline: Priya (cc) will own procurement. We ideally want the pilot to start as early as May (week of 05/04 works) but need the cost ballpark to start approvals.

Thanks — Alex
Alex Jones

alex.jones@nebulapay.com

Karthik / Monica, forwarding the thread and filled scoping sheet from NebulaPay. Key asks:

- They need a ballpark monthly cost for a reserved 4-GPU pool and a firm POC plan for a 2-week pilot starting week of 2026-05-04.
- Technical constraints: p95 <200ms at 300 qps steady, burst to 1k qps for 30–45s, payment routes must be pinned to isolated pool with KMS and audit logs.

Suggested split of work:
- Karthik: initial cost/throughput estimate (include spot vs reserved delta, and an ops runbook for burst behavior). Please include warm-cache strategies and expected warmup time for KV caches.
- Monica: own POC plan and customer onboarding; draft an MSA addendum and coordinate SOC/KMS documentation.

Action items (owner):
1) Karthik: cost/size estimate and recommended autoscale policy (deliver by EOD 2026-04-14).
2) Monica: POC plan, test-cases, and procurement checklist + legal doc template (deliver by 2026-04-15 morning).
3) Soojin: schedule kickoff once estimate and POC plan are ready; confirm start week with customer.

Soojin

Date: 2026-04-15T09:20:00-07:00
Subject: NebulaPay Dedicated POC plan & initial pricing range

Hi Alex / Priya,

Appreciate the scoping sheet and the SOC summary — that made sizing straightforward. Below is a concise POC plan and an initial pricing range you can share with procurement.

POC summary (2 weeks)
- Objective: validate p95 latency and burst handling for payment and non-payment routes with a small subset of production traffic.
- Setup: 4 x A100-equivalent GPUs in a Dedicated reserved pool (isolated). Routes: payment routes pinned to pool; non-payment routed to shared fallback.
- Tests: steady 300 qps baseline; two scripted bursts to 1k qps (45s) with traffic replay; end-to-end audit logging and KMS key rotation test.

Deliverables
- Test plan + runbook
- Perf dashboard access (per-route latency + token cost)
- Post-POC report with recommended production sizing and cost model

Initial pricing range (ballpark, USD/month)
- 4-GPU reserved pool (production): $25k–$32k / month (region: us-east)
- 2-week POC (one-time): $4k–$6k (covers reserved infra + engineering support and runbook)

Notes and caveats
- Final pricing and recommended size will change after we run a short warmup run against your sample prompts (cache warmup materially affects cost).
- If you want lower unit cost we can explore quantized model variants and caching adjustments; Karthik will include those options in the sizing doc.

Next steps
1) If this looks reasonable, Priya please confirm and we will issue an MSA addendum + POC SOW.
2) Karthik and I will run a 30–45 minute technical kickoff (proposed: 2026-05-04 09:00 PT).
3) You sign the POC SOW and provide test credentials / sample traffic (redacted).

Attached: POC plan (link in Drive) and our SOC2 summary.

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call to walk procurement through the line items.

—Monica
